newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares soar 4.32 pct on cash influx.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares soar 4.32 pct on cash influx.

text.p: Istanbul shares surged on Wednesday in active trade led by bluechips and fuelled by cash influx, following Tuesday's 3.72 percent rally, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed at a day's high of 94,304.43, up 3,908.47 points, or 4.32 percent from Tuesday and compared to an all-time high close of 94,407.22 on December 6.
Two-day gains reached 8.2 percent since Monday's 2.44 percent fall prompted by the S&P's dowgrading of Turkey's long-term foreign currency debt rating last Friday.
Trade volume soared to 25.15 trillion lira ($238.3 million) from Tuesday's 19.17 trillion ($182.2 million).
"Part of the cash withdrawn in recent weeks has probably returned to the stock market," said one dealer.

The index had lost 5.37 percent last week amid rumours ahead of the S&P's rating cut and negative sentiment due to cancellation of a law allowing the government to sell state property and failure to overcome stiff resistance at the index's 95,000 mark.
